chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Asadi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Harun ibn Yazeed narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Mi'adh narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Ali ibn Mudrik, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: 'Is it difficult for any of you to recite a third of the Qur'an every night?' They said: 'And who can handle that?' He said: 'Say: He is Allah, Alone' [112:1] three times, which is a third of the Qur'an.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: peace be upon him and his Family
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, Alone (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: How can one recite a third of the Qur'an every night?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to demonstrate the Prophet's pedagogical wisdom in making the obligation of nightly recitation accessible to all companions, regardless of their memorization capacity. By equating Surah Al-Ikhlas with a third of the Qur'an, the tradition highlights the surah's unique theological weight as a concise summary of Tawhid (monotheism), a concept deeply emphasized in Shia exegesis. This practice underscores the balance between spiritual diligence and practical feasibility in daily worship.
